title: Bananas (per lb)

drivers.name: Price increase (1.5%)
drivers.evidence: Historical price elasticity: -1.2% per 1% price rise; noise-adjusted effect on 13 weeks; one prior price change.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 433.5. No events or promotions are scheduled. The price increased 1.5% to $0.68. Historical data shows a 1.2% price elasticity (from past 13 weeks), implying a ~1.3% demand drop. The noise-adjusted estimate for price sensitivity is x0.987. This is supported by one prior price change with a small effect. The evidence is moderate. The baseline already includes seasonal trends and noise. No other drivers. The classical model's 1.00 is not adjusted as it ignores price effects.

brief:
PRODUCT: Bananas (per lb) | category Produce | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-09-28 to 2026-10-04 (next week)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 0.68 (+1.5% vs regular price 0.67)

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 433.5 | 5%-95%: 290.5 - 552.4 | 10%-90%: 332.2 - 525.5

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-29% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
